scope: Opt-in SMT-LIB preprocessing prototype for native FiniteSet. All 1362 inputs preprocessed; matched solving measurements cover 186 inputs.

rules: Eliminate bounded filters whose predicate does not use the bound variable, retaining the domain emptiness condition.
Replace uniquely fixed existential elements by membership and the substituted predicate; handle equalities and equal lower/upper bounds.
For single-field records, reconstruct the unique record from its field value.
Replace universal fixed-point predicates by an empty-or-singleton condition.
Factor independent implication guards in universals and conjunction guards in existentials.
Apply supporting Boolean, arithmetic-zero, singleton-membership and constructor-selector reductions.
prototype.safety: Capture-safe substitution handles nested lambda/quantifier/let binders and quoted aliases. Unknown or overloaded result sorts are not guessed; Real-valued points are not substituted into Int domains. Partial multi-field records and nonzero-width intervals are not collapsed.

measurement.selection: All 138 cvc5-UNSAT cases and 48 evenly sampled cvc5-SAT cases, identical to the earlier validation subset.
measurement.method: Separate sequential batches with the same binary and worker count: preprocessed first, then a fresh unprocessed baseline. No solver C++ code changed for this prototype.
measurement.caveat: Concurrent throughput measurements, not isolated single-process latency. Preprocessing time is reported separately.

solver_workload.note: The median workload decreases substantially, but hard SAT cases still dominate cumulative work and peak memory.

preprocessing_cost.cost_note: Native rewrite timing excludes input parsing and file I/O. Translation timing includes conversion, preprocessing and emission, but excludes source parsing and file I/O.

validation.python_tests: 20 passed, including 19 independent cvc5 unsatisfiability checks of original XOR simplified formulas.
validation.additional_reference_checks: Existing eight semantic cases checked in original cvc5 syntax and both universal encodings.

known_sat_model.note: The original SAT model satisfies both assertion sets even though solving the preprocessed form times out.

native_implementation.proof_mode: Proof-enabled goals skip these rewrites; the SMT solver remains available.

validation.reference_note: Outer universals checked pointwise with fresh constants. cvc5 returns unknown on the case containing an additional unbounded integer quantifier; its native output matches the expected capture-safe substitution.

matched_benchmark.scope: 186 SLEEC cases: all 138 reference-UNSAT cases and 48 evenly sampled reference-SAT cases; not a new full-corpus solve.
matched_benchmark.method: Sequential native-tactic, current-binary default-baseline, and fresh cvc5 batches. Summed process wall times include native preprocessing and timeouts.

native_vs_historical_python_prototype.note: The Python-prototype run is historical, not rerun in this batch.

extremum_preprocessing.rule: Existence of a minimum/maximum of an Int/Real projection over a native finite set is equivalent to nonemptiness.
extremum_preprocessing.safety: Match identical domains and projections with capture-safe lifting; reject strict orders and projections depending on the candidate. Keep the empty-domain guard. Proof-mode behavior and the default solver pipeline are unchanged.
extremum_preprocessing.scope: Same 186-input subset, eight workers, 20-second limit; not a new full-corpus solve.

native_implementation.measurement_note: matched_benchmark records the previous native tactic; extremum_preprocessing records the later extremum-rule run. Previous baseline and cvc5 measurements were not rerun for the extremum comparison.

decision: Keep opt-in via finite-set: extremum preprocessing solves all 48 sampled SAT cases and 135 of 138 UNSAT cases, with 57 gains and no solved-case regressions over the previous native tactic. Three UNSAT cases still time out.
